policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'And Paul, looking stedfastly on the council' renders the name and the dative alike whether the article stands and whichever order the words take; Greek article and word order leave no English trace.

A recitative hoti before the quotation is untranslated in English; ASV 'for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil' reads the same with or without it. The Ex. 22:28 note is a cross-reference, not a textual note.
ASV 'he cried out' is a simple past that renders imperfect ekrazen and aorist ekraxen indifferently.
ASV reads 'a son of Pharisees', a plural genitive answering to Pharisaion; the singular Pharisaiou would give 'a son of a Pharisee'.
English requires the subject pronoun in 'I am a Pharisee' whether or not emphatic ego stands in the Greek; ASV gives it no added weight.
ASV 'And when he had so said' is a general past rendering of the genitive absolute; it fixes neither present lalountos against the aorists nor laleo against lego.
ASV names both parties: 'a dissension between the Pharisees and Sadducees'; the reading omitting kai Saddoukaion leaves the Sadducees unmentioned.
The correlative particle men is untranslated in ASV 'For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection'; its presence or absence leaves no English trace.
ASV 'neither angel, nor spirit' renders mete and mede alike; the two negatives are not distinguished in English.
ASV reads 'some of the scribes of the Pharisees' part', a partitive answering to tines ton grammateon; hoi grammateis would give 'the scribes'.
ASV ends the speech at 'or an angel?' with no rendering of me theomachomen ('let us not fight against God').
ASV 'And when there arose a great dissension' renders the genitive absolute as a past clause; present ginomenes and aorist genomenes are indistinguishable in it.

ASV 'fearing lest Paul should be torn in pieces' fits phobetheis and eulabetheis equally; both are rendered 'fearing'. The verse note concerns 'chief captain' and is an alternative_rendering, which cannot decide a reading.

ASV 'commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force' coordinates two English infinitives, which is the ordinary rendering of the participle kataban with the infinitive as well as of katabenai kai.
The connective te is untranslated in ASV 'and bring him into the castle'; its presence or absence leaves no English trace.
ASV reads 'Be of good cheer:' with no vocative; the added Paule would give 'Be of good cheer, Paul'.
ASV reads 'the Jews banded together', answering to hoi Ioudaioi; tines ton Ioudaion would give 'certain of the Jews'.
ASV 'that made this conspiracy' renders the aorist poiesamenoi and the perfect pepoiekotes alike.
ASV 23:15 has no 'to-morrow' in the council's request; the added aurion is unrendered here, though ASV does render it at 23:20 where the Greek has it.
ASV 'that he bring him down unto you' renders eis hymas and pros hymas alike, and the order of pronoun and verb leaves no English trace.
ASV 'heard of their lying in wait' fits the feminine enedran and the neuter enedron equally; the two forms are the same noun.
ASV 'Bring this young man unto the chief captain' renders apage and apagage alike; the two forms of the same imperative are not distinguished in English.
ASV 'for he hath something to tell him' is unaffected by the order of ti and the infinitive.
ASV 'this young man' renders neanian and neaniskon alike.
ASV 'to bring down Paul to-morrow unto the council' contains every element of both readings; only their Greek order differs.

ASV 'as though thou wouldest inquire somewhat more exactly concerning him' makes the addressee the one inquiring, which English supplies for the neuter mellon as readily as for nominative mellon or accusative mellonta; the participle's case leaves no trace.
ASV 'and now are they ready' is unaffected by the order of eisin and hetoimoi.
ASV 'let the young man go' renders neaniskon and neanian alike.
ASV 'signified these things to me' renders emphatic eme and enclitic me alike.
ASV 'two of the centurions' is unaffected by the order of tinas and dyo.
ASV 'a letter after this form' renders echousan and the compound periechousan alike.

ASV 'and rescued him' supplies the object English idiom requires; the pronoun is unitalicized but not marked, so it does not show whether auton stood in the Greek, and exeilamen and exeilomen are the same aorist.
ASV 'And desiring to know' renders the connective te and de alike.

ASV 'desiring to know the cause' renders epignonai and simple gnonai alike. The verse note concerns the omission of the whole clause by other authorities, which ASV keeps in its text, and does not touch this word.

ASV 'I brought him down unto their council' supplies the object English requires; the pronoun is unmarked and does not show whether auton stood. The verse note reports authorities omitting the clause ASV retains, not this word.
ASV 'whom I found to be accused' carries no connective, so the presence or absence of de leaves no English trace.
ASV 'to have nothing laid to his charge' is unaffected by the order of echonta and enklema.
ASV 'that there would be a plot against the man' renders the future infinitive esesthai, and the added mellein would still be rendered 'would be'.

ASV's text reads 'I sent him to thee forthwith', rendering exautes and lacking any 'by the Jews'. The mapped textual note assigns 'against the man on their part' (ex auton) to other authorities, placing that reading in the margin and not in the text.
ASV 'to speak against him before thee' renders the prepositional phrase with or without the substantivizing article ta.
ASV's text ends the letter at 'before thee', and the mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities add Farewell' assigns Errhoso to the margin.
ASV 'by night' renders dia nyktos with or without the article tes.
ASV 'to go with him' renders aperchesthai and poreuesthai alike.
ASV reads 'he asked of what province he was', carrying the subject over from the previous clause; the added ho hegemon would give 'the governor asked'.
ASV 'of what province' renders eparcheias and eparchias alike; the two are spellings of one noun.
ASV 'and he commanded him to be kept' turns the clause finite, which is the ordinary English rendering of the participle keleusas as well as of the finite ekeleusen te auton.
ASV 'in Herod's palace' renders the genitive with or without the article tou.
ASV 'commanded him to be kept' has an object, but the reading omitting auton here carries the pronoun earlier in the clause, so the English does not show which position it held.
